label: City of Edmonton
note: No separate Edmonton variance form was found; the SCC form is the baseline. Confirm with Safety Codes, Permits and Inspections. Completeness screening only; not a finding about the design.

checks.label: Pre-application meeting booked with Development Services and Safety Codes officers
checks.why: The PAB guide recommends booking a pre-application meeting before submission; for Point Access Block proposals building permit reviewers attend. Recommended, not mandatory.
checks.prompt: Have you booked or held a pre-application meeting?

checks.label: Registered architect and/or engineer involved in design, field review and preparation of the Alternative Solution
checks.why: Professional involvement is a mandatory criterion for Point Access Block applications; plans and specifications must be authenticated per professional practice standards.

checks.label: Alternative Solution prepared by a qualified Fire Protection or Life Safety Code Consultant
checks.why: Applications that put forward a Point Access Block are required to submit an Alternative Solution prepared by such a consultant.

checks.label: Does the alternative solution modify any specific firefighting requirement of the NBC(AE), including Division B, Subsection 3.2.5., or other specific firefighting provisions?
checks.why: If any answer is yes, documentation of the impact on emergency services is required (guideline pp.8-9). This is a screen for the applicant's professional, not a finding about the design.

checks.label: Do the life safety or property protection features of the alternative solution design rely on timely intervention by the local fire service, including for spatial separation/exposure protection?
checks.why: If any answer is yes, documentation of the impact on emergency services is required (guideline pp.8-9). This is a screen for the applicant's professional, not a finding about the design.

checks.label: Does the alternative solution introduce equipment, technology, or processes which are novel to Edmonton Fire Rescue Services, or which may be incompatible with technology and equipment used by responders?
checks.why: If any answer is yes, documentation of the impact on emergency services is required (guideline pp.8-9). This is a screen for the applicant's professional, not a finding about the design.

checks.label: Does the alternative solution require special operational plans for occupants which may affect emergency response and intervention?
checks.why: If any answer is yes, documentation of the impact on emergency services is required (guideline pp.8-9). This is a screen for the applicant's professional, not a finding about the design.

checks.label: Section C functional statements F06, F12 or F13 referenced
checks.why: Any variance which includes reference to Functional Statements F06, F12, or F13 likely impacts emergency services.

checks.label: Is the project outside the Outside 10-minute Boundary (maps.edmonton.ca, layer ERD Public Data)?
checks.why: For projects outside this response area, careful consideration must be given to the impact on spatial separation and on delayed emergency response.

checks.label: Available fire flow confirmed with the EFRS Engineer
checks.why: Specific Available Fire Flow information can be obtained from the EFRS Engineer; designers should verify water supply for firefighters.

checks.label: Swept path analysis for fire apparatus access (only if apparatus access is varied)
checks.why: A swept path analysis conforming to the City of Edmonton Swept Path Analysis guideline ensures access and maneuverability by aerial apparatus.
checks.prompt: Does the variance change fire apparatus access?

checks.label: Inspection, testing and maintenance (ITM) and commissioning documentation for systems introduced by the alternative solution
checks.why: ITM procedures, including commissioning, are required to be provided with documentation of an alternative solution.

checks.label: Documented assumptions and objective demonstration of performance relative to the Division B acceptable solutions
checks.why: Assumptions and limiting factors for affected emergency response are to be documented; conclusions must not rest on judgement without demonstration.

checks.label: Peer review notice: alternative solutions that impact emergency response are reviewed by SCPI and EFRS professionals
checks.why: Practitioners are encouraged to contact the guideline authors before submitting, particularly if assumptions about emergency services are ambiguous.

checks.label: No separate Edmonton variance form was found; the SCC form is the baseline. Confirm with Safety Codes, Permits and Inspections.
checks.why: The supplied Edmonton documents were searched; none contains a separate variance form.
